```{r}

# ============================================================
# DATA 101 CAPSTONE
# INSTITUTIONS: PUBLIC SPENDING VS INCOME INEQUALITY
#
# X-axis:
#   Government Expense (% GDP)
#   Government Education Spending (% GDP)
#
# Y-axis:
#   Income Inequality (SWIID Gini)
#
# Interactive Shiny + Plotly Scatterplot
# ============================================================


# PART 1: PACKAGES

library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)


# PART 2: LOAD DATA

files <- list.files(
  path = ".",
  pattern = "^wdi_clean(\\([0-9]+\\))?\\.csv$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(files) == 0) {
  files <- list.files(
    path = "~",
    pattern = "^wdi_clean(\\([0-9]+\\))?\\.csv$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
}

if (length(files) == 0) {
  stop("Cannot find wdi_clean.csv in your project.")
}

# Prefer the original filename

preferred <- files[
  basename(files) == "wdi_clean.csv"
]

data_path <- if (length(preferred) > 0) {
  preferred[1]
} else {
  files[1]
}

data <- read_csv(
  data_path,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Verify required columns exist

required_columns <- c(
  "country",
  "iso3c",
  "region",
  "year",
  "gov_expense",
  "edc_spending",
  "swiid_gini"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "Missing columns:",
      paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  )
}


# PART 3: CLEAN DATA

graph_data <- data %>%
  transmute(
    country = as.character(country),
    iso3c = as.character(iso3c),
    region = as.character(region),
    year = as.integer(year),

    gov_expense = as.numeric(gov_expense),
    edc_spending = as.numeric(edc_spending),
    swiid_gini = as.numeric(swiid_gini)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(country),
    !is.na(iso3c),
    !is.na(region),
    !is.na(year)
  ) %>%
  distinct(iso3c, year, .keep_all = TRUE)


# PART 4: SAFE SLIDER SETTINGS

# This function prevents NA/NULL slider errors.

safe_max <- function(x, fallback = 100) {

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(fallback)
  }

  max(1, ceiling(max(x)))
}

safe_default <- function(x, fallback = 50) {

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(fallback)
  }

  max(
    1,
    ceiling(
      as.numeric(
        quantile(
          x,
          0.99,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      )
    )
  )
}

# Set slider maximums

x_max <- c(
  gov_expense = safe_max(
    graph_data$gov_expense
  ),

  edc_spending = safe_max(
    graph_data$edc_spending
  )
)

# Set default viewing ranges

x_default <- c(
  gov_expense = safe_default(
    graph_data$gov_expense
  ),

  edc_spending = safe_default(
    graph_data$edc_spending
  )
)

# Ensure defaults are valid

x_default <- pmin(
  x_default,
  x_max
)

# Available years

years <- sort(
  unique(graph_data$year)
)

if (length(years) == 0) {
  stop("No valid years found in dataset.")
}

default_year <- if (2022 %in% years) {
  2022
} else {
  max(years)
}

# Regions and countries

regions <- sort(
  unique(graph_data$region)
)

countries <- sort(
  unique(graph_data$country)
)

# Variable labels

x_choices <- c(
  "Government Expense (% GDP)" = "gov_expense",
  "Government Education Spending (% GDP)" = "edc_spending"
)

x_labels <- c(
  gov_expense = "Government Expense (% of GDP)",
  edc_spending = "Government Education Spending (% of GDP)"
)


# ============================================================
# PART 5: USER INTERFACE
# ============================================================

ui <- fluidPage(

  titlePanel(
    "Public Spending and Income Inequality"
  ),

  p(
    "Explore how public spending relates to income
     inequality across countries and over time."
  ),

  sidebarLayout(

    sidebarPanel(

      # X-AXIS VARIABLE

      selectInput(
        "x_variable",
        "Choose Public Spending Variable:",
        choices = x_choices,
        selected = "gov_expense"
      ),

      # YEAR

      sliderInput(
        "year",
        "Select Year:",
        min = min(years),
        max = max(years),
        value = default_year,
        step = 1,
        sep = ""
      ),

      # REGION

      selectInput(
        "region",
        "Select Region:",
        choices = c(
          "All Regions",
          regions
        ),
        selected = "All Regions"
      ),

      # COUNTRIES

      selectizeInput(
        "countries",
        "Select Countries (Blank = All):",
        choices = countries,
        selected = character(0),
        multiple = TRUE,
        options = list(
          placeholder = "All Countries"
        )
      ),

      # X-AXIS RANGE

      sliderInput(
        "x_range",
        "Public Spending Range (% GDP):",
        min = 0,
        max = unname(x_max["gov_expense"]),
        value = c(
          0,
          unname(x_default["gov_expense"])
        ),
        step = 1
      ),

      # Y-AXIS RANGE

      sliderInput(
        "y_range",
        "Income Inequality Range (Gini):",
        min = 0,
        max = 100,
        value = c(0, 100),
        step = 1
      ),

      # REGRESSION LINE

      checkboxInput(
        "show_trend",
        "Show Regression Line",
        value = TRUE
      ),

      # REGION COLORS

      checkboxInput(
        "color_region",
        "Color Countries by Region",
        value = TRUE
      ),

      # RESET BUTTON

      actionButton(
        "reset",
        "Reset Filters"
      ),

      hr(),

      h4("How to Read This Graph"),

      tags$ul(

        tags$li(
          strong("Each dot: "),
          "Represents one country."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("X-axis: "),
          "Government spending as a percentage of GDP."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("Y-axis: "),
          "Income inequality measured using SWIID Gini."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("Higher Gini: "),
          "Greater income inequality."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("Colors: "),
          "Different world regions."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("Black line: "),
          "The overall linear regression trend."
        ),

        tags$li(
          strong("Pearson r: "),
          "Measures the strength and direction
           of the linear relationship."
        )
      ),

      hr(),

      h4("Data Sources"),

      p("Government Expense: World Bank"),

      p("Education Spending: World Bank"),

      p("Income Inequality: SWIID")
    ),

    mainPanel(

      plotlyOutput(
        "spending_scatter",
        height = "570px"
      ),

      h4("Summary Statistics"),

      fluidRow(

        column(
          4,
          strong(textOutput("country_count"))
        ),

        column(
          4,
          strong(textOutput("correlation"))
        ),

        column(
          4,
          strong(textOutput("average_gini"))
        )
      ),

      hr(),

      h4("Country Data"),

      tableOutput("country_table"),

      hr(),

      h4("Interpretation"),

      textOutput("interpretation"),

      br(),

      p(
        "Note: Correlation does not establish causation."
      )
    )
  )
)


# ============================================================
# PART 6: SERVER
# ============================================================

server <- function(input, output, session) {


  # 6A: UPDATE X-AXIS SLIDER

  observeEvent(input$x_variable, {

    variable <- input$x_variable

    updateSliderInput(
      session,
      "x_range",

      label = paste0(
        x_labels[[variable]],
        " Range:"
      ),

      min = 0,

      max = unname(
        x_max[[variable]]
      ),

      value = c(
        0,
        unname(x_default[[variable]])
      ),

      step = 1
    )
  })


  # 6B: FILTER DATA

  filtered_data <- reactive({

    req(input$x_variable)
    req(input$x_range)
    req(input$y_range)

    df <- graph_data %>%
      mutate(
        x_value = .data[[input$x_variable]]
      ) %>%
      filter(
        year == input$year,
        is.finite(x_value),
        is.finite(swiid_gini),

        x_value >= input$x_range[1],
        x_value <= input$x_range[2],

        swiid_gini >= input$y_range[1],
        swiid_gini <= input$y_range[2]
      )

    if (input$region != "All Regions") {

      df <- df %>%
        filter(
          region == input$region
        )
    }

    if (length(input$countries) > 0) {

      df <- df %>%
        filter(
          country %in% input$countries
        )
    }

    df
  })


  # 6C: CORRELATION

  correlation_value <- reactive({

    df <- filtered_data()

    if (nrow(df) < 3) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    if (
      sd(df$x_value) == 0 ||
      sd(df$swiid_gini) == 0
    ) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    cor(
      df$x_value,
      df$swiid_gini,
      method = "pearson"
    )
  })


  # ==========================================================
  # PART 7: INTERACTIVE SCATTERPLOT
  # ==========================================================

  output$spending_scatter <- renderPlotly({

    df <- filtered_data()

    validate(
      need(
        nrow(df) > 0,
        "No matching countries for this selection.
         Try changing the year or expanding the ranges."
      )
    )

    # Hover information

    df <- df %>%
      mutate(
        Hover = paste0(
          "<b>", country, "</b>",
          "<br>Year: ", year,
          "<br>Region: ", region,
          "<br>", x_labels[[input$x_variable]],
          ": ", round(x_value, 2),
          "<br>SWIID Gini: ",
          round(swiid_gini, 2)
        )
      )

    # Build Plotly scatterplot

    if (input$color_region) {

      p <- plot_ly(
        data = df,

        x = ~x_value,
        y = ~swiid_gini,

        color = ~region,

        text = ~Hover,
        hoverinfo = "text",

        type = "scatter",
        mode = "markers",

        marker = list(
          size = 9,
          opacity = 0.75
        )
      )

    } else {

      p <- plot_ly(
        data = df,

        x = ~x_value,
        y = ~swiid_gini,

        text = ~Hover,
        hoverinfo = "text",

        type = "scatter",
        mode = "markers",

        marker = list(
          size = 9,
          color = "#377EB8",
          opacity = 0.75
        ),

        showlegend = FALSE
      )
    }

    # Regression line

    if (
      input$show_trend &&
      nrow(df) >= 3 &&
      sd(df$x_value) > 0
    ) {

      model <- lm(
        swiid_gini ~ x_value,
        data = df
      )

      trend_x <- seq(
        min(df$x_value),
        max(df$x_value),
        length.out = 100
      )

      trend_y <- predict(
        model,
        newdata = data.frame(
          x_value = trend_x
        )
      )

      p <- p %>%
        add_lines(
          x = trend_x,
          y = trend_y,

          inherit = FALSE,

          line = list(
            color = "black",
            width = 3
          ),

          name = "Regression Line",
          showlegend = FALSE,
          hoverinfo = "skip"
        )
    }

    # Layout

    p %>%
      layout(

        title = list(
          text = paste0(
            x_labels[[input$x_variable]],
            " vs. Income Inequality (",
            input$year,
            ")"
          )
        ),

        xaxis = list(
          title = x_labels[[input$x_variable]],
          range = input$x_range,
          autorange = FALSE
        ),

        yaxis = list(
          title = "Income Inequality (SWIID Gini)",
          range = input$y_range,
          autorange = FALSE
        ),

        hovermode = "closest",

        legend = list(
          title = list(
            text = "Region"
          )
        ),

        margin = list(
          t = 90,
          b = 85,
          l = 85,
          r = 35
        )
      )
  })


  # ==========================================================
  # PART 8: SUMMARY STATISTICS
  # ==========================================================

  output$country_count <- renderText({

    paste(
      "Countries:",
      n_distinct(
        filtered_data()$iso3c
      )
    )
  })


  output$correlation <- renderText({

    r <- correlation_value()

    if (is.na(r)) {
      return("Pearson r: N/A")
    }

    paste0(
      "Pearson r: ",
      sprintf("%.3f", r)
    )
  })


  output$average_gini <- renderText({

    df <- filtered_data()

    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      return("Average Gini: N/A")
    }

    paste0(
      "Average Gini: ",
      round(
        mean(df$swiid_gini),
        2
      )
    )
  })


  # ==========================================================
  # PART 9: COUNTRY DATA TABLE
  # ==========================================================

  output$country_table <- renderTable({

    df <- filtered_data()

    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    df %>%
      arrange(desc(x_value)) %>%
      transmute(
        Country = country,
        Region = region,
        Year = year,

        `Public Spending (% GDP)` = round(
          x_value, 2
        ),

        `SWIID Gini` = round(
          swiid_gini, 2
        )
      )

  }, striped = TRUE, bordered = TRUE)


  # ==========================================================
  # PART 10: AUTOMATIC INTERPRETATION
  # ==========================================================

  output$interpretation <- renderText({

    r <- correlation_value()

    if (is.na(r)) {

      return(
        "There are not enough observations or
         variation to calculate a Pearson correlation."
      )
    }

    strength <- if (abs(r) < 0.2) {
      "very weak"
    } else if (abs(r) < 0.4) {
      "weak"
    } else if (abs(r) < 0.6) {
      "moderate"
    } else if (abs(r) < 0.8) {
      "strong"
    } else {
      "very strong"
    }

    direction <- if (r > 0) {
      "positive"
    } else if (r < 0) {
      "negative"
    } else {
      "no"
    }

    meaning <- if (r > 0) {

      "Higher spending is associated with
       higher income inequality."

    } else if (r < 0) {

      "Higher spending is associated with
       lower income inequality."

    } else {

      "No linear association is detected."
    }

    paste0(
      "For ", input$year,
      ", the selected countries show a ",
      strength, " ", direction,
      " linear association (r = ",
      round(r, 3), "). ",
      meaning,
      " This does not establish causation."
    )
  })


  # ==========================================================
  # PART 11: RESET FILTERS
  # ==========================================================

  observeEvent(input$reset, {

    updateSelectInput(
      session,
      "x_variable",
      selected = "gov_expense"
    )

    updateSliderInput(
      session,
      "year",
      value = default_year
    )

    updateSelectInput(
      session,
      "region",
      selected = "All Regions"
    )

    updateSelectizeInput(
      session,
      "countries",
      selected = character(0)
    )

    updateSliderInput(
      session,
      "x_range",
      min = 0,
      max = unname(x_max["gov_expense"]),
      value = c(
        0,
        unname(x_default["gov_expense"])
      )
    )

    updateSliderInput(
      session,
      "y_range",
      value = c(0, 100)
    )

    updateCheckboxInput(
      session,
      "show_trend",
      value = TRUE
    )

    updateCheckboxInput(
      session,
      "color_region",
      value = TRUE
    )
  })

}


# ============================================================
# PART 12: RUN SHINY APP
# ============================================================

shinyApp(
  ui = ui,
  server = server
)

```
